rationale:
Split into 4 children: three leaves plus pairing_bound, which depends on coord_bound.

Why split. The supplied 9-step proof bundles four separable obligations, each a genuine reusable fact about Simon's objects, around an ε-approximation. Only the selected node can perform that approximation, because children may depend only on one another while mass_bound, mollify and covector_expansion are resolved dependencies of the selected node alone.
- coord_bound (Step 1(i)): |α(e_β)| ≤ |α|.
- norm_add_le (Step 1(ii)): the Euclidean coefficient norm is subadditive. SimonGMT only has covectorEuclideanNorm_zero, _nonneg and _neg; rg finds no existing coordinate bound or triangle inequality.
- coeff_integrable (Steps 2–3, part (a) of the supplied proof): testing IsMeasureRepresentation with χ·dx^β shows every coefficient v^β := euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v ·) β is μ-integrable on each compact K ⊆ W, for W open with W ⊆ U. This is Simon's remark after (2.7), recorded in the frozen IsMeasureRepresentation docstring.
- pairing_bound (Step 5, depends on coord_bound): for continuous θ vanishing off a measurable K with |θ| ≤ D, the coordinate pairing Σ_β θ(x)(e_β)·v^β(x) is μ-integrable, and |∫| ≤ D·Σ_β ∫_K |v^β| dμ.

How the selected node follows by the supplied proof:
- Step 2: CompactlyContainedOpen makes tsupport ω compact and ⊆ W. exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure gives an open V ⊇ tsupport ω with closure V compact and ⊆ W.
- Step 3: apply coeff_integrable with K := closure V. G := Σ_β ∫_{closure V} |v^β| dμ ≥ 0 replaces Σ_β ∫|g_β| dμ. It is at most that constant, since g_β = v(χ dx^β) = v^β on closure V, and plays the same role.
- Step 4: covector_expansion and linearity of v(x) give v(x)(α) = Σ_β α(e_β)·v^β(x) for all x, α.
- Step 5: apply pairing_bound with K := closure V (closed, hence measurable). Then v(θ) is μ-integrable and |∫v(θ)dμ| ≤ D·G.
- Steps 6–9 verbatim:
  - θ := ω gives integrability;
  - mollify gives η with tsupport η ⊆ V;
  - norm_add_le and covectorEuclideanNorm_neg give |η| ≤ C + ε;
  - mass_bound gives |T(η)| ≤ B(C + ε);
  - θ := ω − η gives |∫v(ω)dμ| ≤ B(C + ε) + εG;
  - take ε := ε₀/(B + G + 1) and finish with le_of_forall_pos_le_add.

subproblems.title: A covector coordinate is bounded by the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every n-covector α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n and every strictly increasing multi-index β ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P (an order embedding Fin n ↪o Fin P): |α(e_β)| ≤ |α|. Here α(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β = α(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}) with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1, and |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing]·α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)})²) with b_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n) (β : SimonMultiIndex n P), |euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 1(i).

1. By definition covectorEuclideanNorm α = √S, where S := Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} a_I. Here a_I := (α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)}))² if I is strictly increasing and a_I := 0 otherwise, with b_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. Every a_I is ≥ 0, being a square or 0.
2. For every i, EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply).
3. Put I₀ := (j ↦ β j) : Fin n → Fin P. Since β is an order embedding, I₀ is strictly increasing (OrderEmbedding.strictMono). By Steps 1–2, a_{I₀} = (α(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}))² = c², where c := euclideanCovectorCoordinate α β = α(fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.single (β j) 1) by definition.
4. All summands of S are nonnegative, so one summand is at most the sum: c² = a_{I₀} ≤ S (Finset.single_le_sum over Finset.univ).
5. Hence |c| = √(c²) ≤ √S = covectorEuclideanNorm α, by Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs and the monotonicity of √ (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt). ∎

(Edge cases: for n = 0 the unique empty tuple is strictly increasing and the argument is unchanged. If n > P, then SimonMultiIndex n P is empty and the statement is vacuous.)
proof_key_steps: Unfold |α| = √S, where S sums [I strictly increasing]·α(b_I)² over all I : Fin n → Fin P; every summand is ≥ 0.
I₀ := (j ↦ β j) is strictly increasing and basisFun i = single i 1, so the I₀-summand equals α(e_β)².
A single nonnegative summand is ≤ the sum, so |α(e_β)| = √(α(e_β)²) ≤ √S = |α|.

subproblems.title: Triangle inequality for the Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and all α, γ ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n: |α + γ| ≤ |α| + |γ|. Here |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. |α| = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [I strictly increasing]·α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)})²) with b_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α γ : Covector (Eucl P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (α + γ) ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm γ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 1(ii).

1. Let N := Fin n → Fin P, a finite type, and b_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. Define the coefficient-vector map c : Covector (Eucl P) n → EuclideanSpace ℝ N by c(a)_I := a(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(n−1)}) if I is strictly increasing and c(a)_I := 0 otherwise. In Lean: c(a) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I ↦ if StrictMono I then a (fun i ↦ b (I i)) else 0).
2. For every a, covectorEuclideanNorm a = ‖c(a)‖. Indeed ‖c(a)‖ = √(Σ_I ‖c(a)_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). For each I, ‖c(a)_I‖² = a(b_I)² if I is strictly increasing and = 0 otherwise. This is exactly the I-th summand in the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm a, so the two square roots agree.
3. c is additive: c(α + γ) = c(α) + c(γ). For strictly increasing I, (α + γ)(b_I) = α(b_I) + γ(b_I), because evaluation of continuous alternating maps is additive in the map. For the other I, both sides are 0 = 0 + 0. In Lean, combine the two toLp vectors (WithLp.toLp_add) and compare coordinatewise, splitting on StrictMono I.
4. By the triangle inequality in the normed space EuclideanSpace ℝ N (norm_add_le): covectorEuclideanNorm (α + γ) = ‖c(α) + c(γ)‖ ≤ ‖c(α)‖ + ‖c(γ)‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm γ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coefficient vector c(a) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) with c(a)_I = [I strictly increasing]·a(b_I).
covectorEuclideanNorm a = ‖c(a)‖, comparing summands under EuclideanSpace.norm_eq.
Apply norm_add_le in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).

subproblems.title: Coefficients of a measure representation are integrable on compact subsets (testing with χ·dx^β)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U, W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open and W ⊆ U. Let T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, μ a measure on ℝ^P and v : ℝ^P → NVector (Eucl P) n with IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v: for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, x ↦ v(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable and T(ω) = ∫ v(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x). Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact with K ⊆ W, and let β ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P. Then the coefficient function x ↦ euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β = v(x)(dx^β) is μ-integrable on K (IntegrableOn … K μ). Here dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen W → W ⊆ U → ∀ (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v → ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → ∀ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, IntegrableOn (fun x => euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β) K μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Steps 2–3: the cutoff χ equal to 1 on the relevant compact set, and the test forms χ·dx^β.

1. (Intermediate open set.) ℝ^P is locally compact and regular, K is compact, W is open and K ⊆ W. By exists_open_between_and_isCompact_closure there is an open V₂ with K ⊆ V₂, closure(V₂) ⊆ W and closure(V₂) compact.
2. (Cutoff.) K is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed. Apply exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff to the open set V₂ and the closed set K ⊆ V₂, with smoothness order ∞; ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space. In Lean, ∞ is obtained by setting the lemma's named smoothness argument to ⊤ : ℕ∞; that argument has nothing to do with the form degree n. This gives χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with:
- χ is C^∞, i.e. ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) χ;
- range χ ⊆ [0,1] and support χ = V₂;
- χ(x) = 1 ⇔ x ∈ K for every x.
3. (Test form.) Let dx^β := wedgeCovectors n (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (β j)) ∈ Covector (Eucl P) n and ψ(x) := χ(x)·dx^β.
- ψ is C^∞ as the product of the C^∞ scalar function χ with a constant (ContDiff.smul, contDiff_const). IsSmoothForm means ContDiff ℝ ∞ with ∞ = ↑(⊤ : ℕ∞), which matches Step 2.
- By tsupport_smul_subset_left, tsupport ψ ⊆ tsupport χ = closure(support χ) = closure(V₂). tsupport ψ is closed and lies in the compact set closure(V₂), so it is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset); that is, ψ has compact support.
- tsupport ψ ⊆ closure(V₂) ⊆ W ⊆ U.
Hence ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n, whose membership condition is (ContDiff ℝ ∞ ψ ∧ HasCompactSupport ψ) ∧ tsupport ψ ⊆ U.
4. (Integrability from the representation.) By IsMeasureRepresentation T μ v applied to ψ, g(x) := v(x)(ψ(x)) is μ-integrable. In particular g is μ-integrable on K (Integrable.integrableOn).
5. (Identification on K.) For x ∈ K, χ(x) = 1 by Step 2, so ψ(x) = 1·dx^β = dx^β. Hence g(x) = v(x)(dx^β) = euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β, by the definition of euclideanNVectorCoordinate. K is closed, hence a Borel measurable set. If two functions agree on a measurable set and one is integrable on it, so is the other (IntegrableOn.congr_fun). So x ↦ euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β is μ-integrable on K. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose an open V₂ with K ⊆ V₂, closure V₂ compact and closure V₂ ⊆ W.
Take a smooth cutoff χ with values in [0,1], support χ = V₂ and χ = 1 exactly on K.
ψ := χ·dx^β ∈ TestFormOn U n: it is smooth and tsupport ψ ⊆ closure V₂, which is compact and ⊆ W ⊆ U.
IsMeasureRepresentation makes x ↦ v(x)(ψ(x)) μ-integrable, hence integrable on K.
On the closed (measurable) set K, v(x)(ψ(x)) = v(x)(dx^β), so IntegrableOn transfers to the coefficient function.

subproblems.title: L∞–L¹ estimate for the coordinate pairing of a continuous form vanishing off K
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, v : ℝ^P → NVector (Eucl P) n and K ⊆ ℝ^P a measurable set such that, for every β ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P, the coefficient function v^β(x) := euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β is μ-integrable on K. Let θ : ℝ^P → Covector (Eucl P) n be continuous with θ(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K. Let D ∈ ℝ with |θ(x)| ≤ D for every x (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm). Put f(x) := Σ_{β ∈ SimonMultiIndex n P} θ(x)(e_β)·v^β(x), where θ(x)(e_β) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate (θ x) β. Then f is μ-integrable and |∫ f dμ| ≤ D · Σ_β ∫_K |v^β| dμ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (v : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (K : Set (Eucl P)), MeasurableSet K → (∀ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, IntegrableOn (fun x => euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β) K μ) → ∀ (θ : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n) (D : ℝ), Continuous θ → (∀ x, x ∉ K → θ x = 0) → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (θ x) ≤ D) → Integrable (fun x => ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate (θ x) β * euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β) μ ∧ |∫ x, ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate (θ x) β * euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β ∂μ| ≤ D * ∑ β : SimonMultiIndex n P, ∫ x in K, |euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β| ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Step 5 (integrability and basic estimate), with the coefficient functions of v taken on K.

Sibling used: coord_bound (cmb_rb_abs_euclideanCovectorCoordinate_le).

Notation:
- c_β(x) := euclideanCovectorCoordinate (θ x) β = θ(x)(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}), with e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1;
- v^β(x) := euclideanNVectorCoordinate (v x) β;
- μ_K := μ.restrict K, so that 'μ-integrable on K' means μ_K-integrable and ∫_K means ∫ … ∂μ_K.

1. (Coefficient bounds.) For all β and x, |c_β(x)| ≤ |θ(x)| ≤ D, by the sibling coord_bound applied to θ(x) and β, and the hypothesis.
2. (Continuity.) For fixed β, the map α ↦ α(e_{β(0)}, …, e_{β(n−1)}) is a continuous linear map Covector (Eucl P) n → ℝ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.single (β j) 1)). So c_β, its composition with the continuous θ, is continuous. Hence c_β is AEStronglyMeasurable for μ_K (Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable; ℝ^P is second countable and carries its Borel σ-algebra).
3. (Integrability on K.) By hypothesis each v^β is μ_K-integrable. A bounded a.e.-strongly measurable factor times an integrable function is integrable (Integrable.bdd_mul, using Steps 1–2 with bound D). So each c_β·v^β is μ_K-integrable, and so is the finite sum f (integrable_finsetSum). That is, f is μ-integrable on K.
4. (Vanishing off K.) If x ∉ K then θ(x) = 0. The zero alternating map evaluates to 0, so c_β(x) = 0 for every β and f(x) = 0. Hence support f ⊆ K.
- f is μ-integrable (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset); this is the first conclusion.
- ∫ f dμ = ∫_K f dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
5. (Pointwise bound.) For every x, |f(x)| ≤ Σ_β |c_β(x)|·|v^β(x)| ≤ Σ_β D·|v^β(x)|. This uses Finset.abs_sum_le_sum_abs, |ab| = |a|·|b|, Step 1 and |v^β(x)| ≥ 0. Each x ↦ D·|v^β(x)| is μ_K-integrable (Integrable.abs, Integrable.const_mul), hence so is their finite sum.
6. (Integral estimate.) The following chain uses abs_integral_le_integral_abs, integral_mono (with the integrability from Steps 3 and 5 and the pointwise bound of Step 5), integral_finsetSum, integral_const_mul and Finset.mul_sum:
|∫ f dμ| = |∫_K f dμ| ≤ ∫_K |f| dμ ≤ ∫_K Σ_β D·|v^β| dμ = Σ_β D·∫_K |v^β| dμ = D · Σ_β ∫_K |v^β| dμ.
This is the second conclusion. ∎

(If D < 0 the hypothesis |θ(x)| ≤ D cannot hold, since covectorEuclideanNorm is nonnegative. The argument above never needs D ≥ 0.)
proof_key_steps: x ↦ θ(x)(e_β) is continuous (evaluation is a continuous linear map), hence a.e.-strongly measurable.
Integrable.bdd_mul and finite sums: f is μ-integrable on K.
f = 0 off K, so f is μ-integrable and ∫ f dμ = ∫_K f dμ.
|∫_K f| ≤ ∫_K Σ_β D|v^β| = D · Σ_β ∫_K |v^β| dμ.
